claims.text: Selective chemical dealloying of an NM-HEA precursor can produce a three-dimensional nanoframework.
The dealloying method exploits preferential dissolution of less noble elements.
The precursor is a homogeneous NM-HEA containing noble and less noble metals in a dense alloy configuration.
A controlled acidic solution can preferentially dissolve the less noble metallic components of the NM-HEA.
Dealloying conditions can be optimized to remove less noble metals without corroding the noble-metal framework.
Selective dealloying creates a porous, interconnected three-dimensional nanoframework with nanoscale channels.
The surface of the resulting nanoframework is enriched in noble metals.
Preferential leaching of less noble elements creates voids that develop into a three-dimensional porous structure.
The residual porous network is enriched in catalytically active noble-metal sites.
The dealloyed nanoframework will have a significantly higher specific surface area than the original dense NM-HEA precursor.
The dealloyed nanoframework will exhibit improved catalytic performance relative to the original dense NM-HEA precursor.
The untreated uniform NM-HEA has lower surface area and lower catalytic-site exposure than the proposed dealloyed material.
The method is expected to work when the noble and less noble elements have a clear electrochemical-potential difference.
Insufficient electrochemical differences between constituent elements may prevent selective dissolution.
